name: KEY CONTROL
author: izicubed
description: Physical two-key USB button keyboards AND phone-based cloud judges as per-pilot lap marshals, with two work modes. MANUAL: the timer's own RSSI laps are suppressed - every lap comes from the buttons (key 1 adds, key 2 deletes). SEMI: the timer counts laps as usual and presses confirm them inside a +-threshold window (default 2 s, editable in the panel header) - green = confirmed, yellow = unconfirmed timer lap, blue = button press with no timer lap (a manual lap is added at the press), red = deleted (strikethrough time). Keyboards are read by a forwarder script on a remote Raspberry Pi and forwarded over Socket.IO; the plugin can re-point the forwarder at itself via the Key Control IP setting (forwarder control endpoint on port 8737, URL persisted). Cloud judges: switch on Cloud judges and the plugin opens a room on the judge relay (https://judge.airmode.app by default) and prints one phone link per occupied seat - each judge gets ADD LAP / REMOVE LAP for exactly one pilot. The timer dials out, so no port forwarding, public IP or inbound firewall rule is needed, and each tap carries its own age so relay latency never moves a lap time. Keyboard N maps to the Nth occupied seat of the current heat (R1/R3/R6/R8 -> KB1..KB4), with fixed-seat overrides and a panel-driven Calibrate flow that binds keyboards to channels by pressing a key on each in turn. Each half switches off independently from the panel footer, and a half that is off leaves the panel entirely. Both judge pages carry the live race clock. Works on RotorHazard 4.4+.
